classes.title: The product this repository builds
classes.covers: The Host, the CLI, the desktop shell, the runtime SDK and transport, the protocol, and every crate in this workspace, with the committed artifacts it ships.
classes.boundary: Not the third-party dependencies it links, not the packs, extensions or catalog entries it loads, and not any hosted service: each of those is another class below, and a dependency's licence is its own author's.
classes.why: No LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file is present and `[workspace.package] publish = false`, so no licence has been selected. Selecting one is the act this issue owes; this record states the boundary it must fit.

classes.title: Packs and adapters published by this project
classes.covers: The harness packs, provider adapters and fixtures this project publishes under its own name, separate from the upstream harness or provider they integrate.
classes.boundary: Not the upstream tool they integrate: an adapter's licence grants nothing about the CLI or service it drives, and the upstream's terms continue to govern its own binary and account.
classes.why: No pack or adapter is published yet, so nothing is licensed; the boundary is stated so that the first one is licensed deliberately rather than by default.

classes.title: Third-party extensions, skills, hooks and MCP servers
classes.covers: Loading and running them, and the trust decision that gates it, not their content.
classes.boundary: Not the extension's own code: this project grants no rights over it and takes none. Its licence is its publisher's, and being loadable is not being endorsed, supported or distributed by this project.
classes.why: The published form of the extension SDK, its permission model and its revocation path are #431's; until that lands the class has no artifact to license.

classes.title: Catalog entries describing packs and extensions
classes.covers: The metadata this project publishes about loadable artifacts: name, publisher, version, permissions, signature and the pointer to the artifact.
classes.boundary: Not the artifact it points at: metadata is a pointer, and a catalog entry must not imply a licence, a support level or a distribution right the referenced artifact's publisher has not granted.
classes.why: The catalog and its manifest schema are #431's; this class records that metadata and artifact are separate licensing boundaries before either exists.

classes.title: Optional hosted services
classes.covers: Any service this project operates: the extension registry, telemetry intake, sync or entitlement. Each is optional and each is separate from the code.
classes.boundary: Not the local product: running the Host must never require a hosted service, and a service's terms of use are separate from the licence of the code that talks to it.
classes.why: No hosted service exists in this tree, so nothing is offered under terms; #459 owns bounded telemetry storage and its optional upload, which is the first one planned.

obligations.requirement: Projects, source, prompts, logs and private configuration remain user-owned local data, and the product runs without a hosted service.
A resource is authorized by the local owner before it is used, that consent is bound to exact bytes, and it expires and revokes rather than persisting by default.
No code or prompt leaves the machine without an explicit, inspectable consent; an unconfigured telemetry state is unknown rather than assumed on.
Telemetry is opt-in, with exact event schemas, local inspection, retention and deletion controls, and permission filtering before any aggregation.
obligations.why: No telemetry is transmitted by this tree, so there is nothing to make opt-in yet: #459 owns bounded telemetry storage, retention, privacy and optional upload, and #374 the opt-in product telemetry surface.

obligations.requirement: Hosted services are optional; local-first operation is the default rather than a degraded mode.
obligations.why: No hosted service is operated and no client calls one; #374 owns the observability surface that would be the first, and this issue owns the terms it must be offered under.

obligations.requirement: An extension names a verified publisher, and the trust decision is made per publisher and per version rather than per catalog entry.
obligations.why: Publisher identity needs the extension SDK and registry that #431 owns; nothing in this tree publishes or loads an extension yet.

obligations.requirement: Artifacts are signed by their publisher and the signature is verified before the artifact is trusted, with the release-signing keys held by the maintainers.
obligations.why: Signing is not implemented for extensions or releases: #431 owns the signed extension SDK and #434 the signed release artifacts, installers and update feeds.

obligations.requirement: An extension declares its permissions, the trust level and permissions are visible before installation, and installed code cannot grant itself more.
obligations.why: The permission model ships with the extension SDK and marketplace (#431). The consent ledger here records what the local owner authorized, which is not an extension permission model.

obligations.requirement: A publisher, a version or a vulnerable package can be revoked, and revocation reaches an installed artifact rather than only the catalog.
obligations.why: The resource consent ledger revokes consent for a resource, not a publisher or a catalog entry; publisher and version revocation are #431's with the release channel's revocation in #434.

obligations.requirement: A vulnerability in an extension, a pack or a dependency has a published response path: how it is triaged, what users are told, and how the affected version is withdrawn.
obligations.why: The response path needs the trust model (#191) and the revocation mechanism (#431); the coordinated-disclosure half of it is this issue's own remaining work.

obligations.requirement: Contribution terms are stated: what a contributor grants, how a change is proposed and reviewed, and what a contribution's licence is.
obligations.why: No CONTRIBUTING file or contributor agreement exists. This is this issue's own remaining work and depends on the core licence being selected first.

obligations.requirement: Trademark and naming expectations are stated: what may be called Symbiote, what a fork may call itself, and what a pack or extension may claim.
obligations.why: No trademark policy exists. It is this issue's own remaining work and is independent of the code licence.

obligations.requirement: Fork expectations are stated: what a fork may do, what it must not imply, and how it stays distinguishable from this project.
obligations.why: The licence selected for the core class will answer part of this; the naming and support half is this issue's own remaining work.

obligations.requirement: Commercial hosting expectations are stated: whether a third party may operate this product or a hosted derivative, and under what terms.
obligations.why: No hosted service exists to be operated by anyone; the expectation is this issue's own remaining work and must be stated before the first one is offered.

obligations.requirement: A security report has a private path to the maintainers and a coordinated-disclosure expectation, stated before public beta.
obligations.why: No SECURITY file or security contact exists. #191 owns the threat model; the reporting channel and its expectations are this issue's own remaining work.

obligations.requirement: Every third-party dependency this workspace links is recorded with the licence it is used under, and a licence the distribution boundary cannot honour is refused in CI.
Every committed artifact this repository generates names the program that wrote it, the command that re-derives it and the case that holds it.

levels.rule: May change or be removed in any release; no migration is promised, and a change may be recorded in the contract document's own text without a version gate.
A breaking change needs a major version and a stated migration in the contract document; only permitted once the workspace version is at least 1.0.
Still present and still supported for the stated window, with the replacement named in the contract document; only permitted once the workspace version is at least 1.0.
